title: U.S. House · California's 15th Congressional District
area: San Mateo County on the San Francisco Peninsula, including South San Francisco, San Mateo, and East Palo Alto.

context.text: This district's boundaries changed under California Proposition 50, the mid-decade congressional redistricting measure voters approved in November 2025. Incumbent Kevin Mullin and Republican Charles Hoelter advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary, defeating Anthony Dang, Mantosh Kumar, and Jim Garrity.

candidates.name: Kevin Mullin
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 2, 2026 top-two primary with about 65% of the vote.
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative for California's 15th Congressional District (since 2023); previously California State Assembly (2012-2022)

summary.text: Kevin Mullin is the Democratic incumbent representing California's 15th Congressional District on the San Francisco Peninsula. He previously served a decade in the California State Assembly and founded a communications business before being elected to Congress in 2022.

background.text: Born in San Mateo County, California; graduated from Junipero Serra High School. Earned a bachelor's degree in communications from the University of San Francisco and a master's degree in public administration from San Francisco State University.
Founded KM2 Communications before entering politics.
Served in the California State Assembly and, while there, helped secure record levels of state child-care funding and streamlined the process for obtaining a child-care license.

priorities.text: Says addressing housing affordability and the production of new housing is one of his major priorities, citing his support for the Low-Income Housing Tax Credit program and his authorship of the Weatherization Resilience and Adaptation Program (WRAP) Act.
Says he is focused on reducing the cost of living, citing his introduction of the Poverty Line Act to update how the federal poverty line is calculated.
Says he is a member of the Medicare for All Caucus and a cosponsor of the Medicare for All Act of 2023.

positions.summary: Cosponsors the Medicare for All Act of 2023 and is a member of the Medicare for All Caucus; says the country must continue reducing prescription drug costs and cap the price of drugs like insulin.
Cosponsors the Women's Health Protection Act, which would restore and protect access to abortion nationally, and the EACH Act to repeal the Hyde Amendment.
positions.quote: I unequivocally believe in a woman's right to choose and will continue fighting against policies that restrict access to reproductive health care.

positions.summary: Is a member of the Congressional Renters Caucus and co-led the Prevent Homelessness Act and Eviction Protection Act.
Supports strengthening the Low-Income Housing Tax Credit program and cosponsored the Affordable Housing Credit Improvement Act to expand affordable housing production.
Says he supports a progressive, equitable tax code that asks large corporations and the wealthiest 1% to pay their fair share while keeping costs down for working families.
Cosponsored the Child Care for Every Community Act, which would establish universal child care and early learning programs, and is advocating to fund childcare programs in Congress.

record.text: Assigned to the House Committee on Natural Resources and the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology (Investigations and Oversight Subcommittee) in the 118th Congress (2023-2024).
Introduced the Poverty Line Act and the Weatherization Resilience and Adaptation Program (WRAP) Act as some of his first bills in Congress.
Served in the California State Assembly from 2012 to 2022 before his election to Congress.

candidates.name: Charles Hoelter
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 2, 2026 top-two primary with about 18% of the vote.

summary.text: Charles Hoelter is a San Mateo-based Republican candidate for California's 15th Congressional District. His campaign site describes him as a conservative advocate for "freedom, faith, and family" who has spent years listening to concerns from working families, small business owners, veterans, and law enforcement.

background.text: Graduated from Lincoln High School; earned a bachelor's degree from San Francisco State University in 1989.
Career experience includes working as a supervisor.

priorities.text: Campaign site lists topic areas including energy independence, veterans, Second Amendment rights, education, public safety, border security, and the economy and inflation, though detailed position statements were not posted on the site as of the research date.

candidates.researchNotes: Charles Hoelter's campaign website lists issue-area headings (energy independence, veterans, Second Amendment, education, public safety, border security, economy) but the pages under each contained only placeholder boilerplate text, not substantive position statements, as of the research date. No Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey response was found.
